OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) lead complex end-to-end deployments of frontier models in production alongside our most strategic customers. You will own discovery, technical scoping, system design, build, and production rollout, partnering directly with customer engineering and domain teams.

You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven feedback that changes product and model roadmaps. You’ll work closely with our Product, Research, Partnerships, GRC, Security, and GTM teams.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role you will

  • Own technical delivery across multiple deployments from first prototype to stable production

  • Build full-stack systems that deliver customer value and sharpen how we learn

  • Embed closely with customer teams, understand their needs, and guide adoption of what you build

  • Scope work, sequence delivery, and remove blockers early

  • Make trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality; adjust plans to protect delivery

  • Contribute directly in the code when progress or clarity depends on it

  • Codify working patterns into tools, playbooks, or building blocks that others can use

  • Share field feedback that helps Research and Product understand where the models succeed and where they can improve

  • Keep teams moving through clarity and follow-through

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience that includes customer-facing work

  • Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous environments

  • Write and review production-grade code across frontend and backend using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks

  • Have built or deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behaviour affects product experience

  • Simplify complexity and make fast, sound decisions under pressure

  • Communicate clearly with engineers, product teams, and customer stakeholders

  • Spot risks early and adjust without slowing down

  • Model calm and judgment when the stakes are high

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

raw_data.title: Android Engineer, Plugin Developer Platform
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Plugin Developer Platform team builds the APIs, SDKs, and tools that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, connectors, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and interactive apps.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work covers plugin creation and publishing, the systems that run plugins across our products, and open standards that developers can build on.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Android engineer to bring plugins, connectors, and interactive apps to life on mobile. You’ll build the Android experiences and platform foundations that help developers extend ChatGPT and help users discover and use those capabilities from their devices.

You’ll work across native Android interfaces, developer-facing APIs, and the systems that support extensibility on mobile. You’ll collaborate closely with product, design, and platform engineers, owning features from early exploration through implementation, launch, and iteration.

You’ll also engage directly with developers and partners to understand how their workflows translate to Android. Their experience will inform the interfaces and abstractions you build, the problems you prioritize, and the tradeoffs you make.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Build Android experiences for plugins, connectors, and interactive apps within ChatGPT.

  • Develop reusable Android components and interfaces that support a growing ecosystem of developer-built experiences.

  • Partner with platform engineers to connect native mobile experiences with APIs, SDKs, and backend systems.

  • Work with developers and partners to identify integration challenges and improve the experience of building for mobile.

  • Improve app performance, reliability, architecture, testing, and developer tooling.

  • Own projects from initial requirements through release, measurement, and iteration.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have deep experience building Android applications using Kotlin and modern Android development frameworks.

  • Have shipped consumer-facing mobile products at scale and care deeply about performance, quality, and user experience.

  • Bring a platform mindset and enjoy designing reusable interfaces and abstractions that other developers build on.

  • Enjoy collaborating across engineering, product, and design, and working directly with developers and partners.

  • Are excited about bringing AI-powered tools and extensible experiences to mobile.

  • Thrive in fast-moving environments where you help define both product and technical direction.

raw_data.title: Software Engineer, Life Sciences
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the team

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.

We’re building platforms that connect model intelligence with practical scientific workflows. Our work covers workflows from next-gen sequencing analysis to designing new drugs, helping scientists run computational workloads as well as access laboratory services. By making these capabilities more accessible and useful, we aim to improve early discovery and support downstream progress in drug development.

About the role

We’re looking for experienced full-stack product engineers with strong backend skills to join our growing Life Sciences team.

This is an individual contributor role with substantial ownership. You’ll help define products, design systems, and ship experiences that connect scientists with AI capabilities and laboratory workflows. You’ll work across the stack, partnering with researchers, scientists, and infrastructure engineers to turn complex needs into reliable, intuitive products.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, product judgment, and experience shipping to large user bases. Life sciences experience is helpful, but you don’t need a scientific background to make a meaningful contribution.

In this role, you will

  • Design backend services, APIs, and integrations that connect users with models, scientific tools, and laboratory services.

  • Create intuitive interfaces that help scientists navigate complex workflows.

  • Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, operation, and iteration.

  • Work with scientific and research partners to identify user needs and prioritize valuable product improvements.

  • Partner with dedicated infrastructure engineers on performance, reliability, and scaling.

  • Make thoughtful engineering decisions that balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals and depth in backend development, alongside the ability to build across the stack.

  • Have shipped and operated products used by large user bases.

  • Bring strong product sense and can translate ambiguous needs into useful software.

  • Work autonomously, make sound technical decisions, and drive projects forward with limited direction.

  • Enjoy hands-on building and taking ownership within a lean team.

  • Are excited about advances in AI and how they could change scientific work.

  • Learn unfamiliar domains quickly and collaborate effectively with scientific and technical partners.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Building AI applications, model-serving integrations, or inference platforms.

  • Developing marketplaces or products that coordinate services and complex workflows.

  • Taking new products from early concepts through launch and adoption.

  • Working with scientific tools, research data, or laboratory systems.

raw_data.title: Deployment Lead, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) - Platform
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. Within FDE, the Platform team turns promising use cases into repeatable solutions to deliver at scale.

About the Role

As a foundational Platform Deployment Lead (DL), you’ll shape new solutions and lead them from customer validation through launch and repeatable adoption. You’ll combine product judgment with hands-on customer deployment experience to identify valuable problems and define a path to scale. You’ll also help build the function, navigating significant ambiguity to define its scope and ways of working.

You’ll partner with FDEs, Product, and GTM to align the roadmap, resolve shared dependencies, and balance customer commitments with reusable capabilities.

Success means measurable customer and business impact, growing adoption, and building solutions that field teams or partners can deliver without depending on the originating team.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York City, with 3 days in the office per week, relocation assistance, and travel up to 50%.

In this role, you will:

  • Define clear solutions around a valuable problem and shape the path to market.

  • Use customer, field learnings, and market evidence to set the next proof point, narrow scope, and recommend where to invest.

  • Select design partners and use pilots to test value and repeatability.

  • Define quality and launch criteria.

  • Enable field teams and partners to scope, sell, and deliver the solution using playbooks and building the support model they need.

  • Track adoption and establish ongoing ownership as solutions scale.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 5+ years of product leadership or customer-facing technical delivery experience.

  • Have taken technical products from discovery through production and adoption.

  • Translate customer workflows and deployment evidence into clear product priorities.

  • Can reason through integrations, data, evaluations, and enterprise deployment constraints.

  • Thrive in ambiguity and enjoy building new functions: creating structure where little exists, making sound decisions with incomplete information, and adapting as priorities evolve.

  • Build trust and drive decisions across engineering, Product, GTM, partners, and customers.

  • Understand technical go-to-market and enjoy building new solutions in ambiguous environments.

OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

  • Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

jobs.title: 🔥 Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices

raw_data.title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.

A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.

You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.

This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.

In This Role, You Will

  • Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

  • Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

  • Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

  • Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

  • Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

  • Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

  • Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

  • Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

  • Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

  • Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

  • Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

  • Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

  • Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

  • Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

  • Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

  • Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

  • Experience developing one or more of the following:

    • HSM firmware or trusted applications

    • Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services

    • HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware

    • PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations

    • Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols

    • HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems

    • Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

  • Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

  • Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

  • Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

  • Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

  • The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

  • Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.

Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

  • Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

  • Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

  • Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

  • Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

  • Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

  • Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

  • Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

  • Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

  • Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

  • Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

raw_data.title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Munich. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

  • Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

  • Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

  • Are fluent in both German and English

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

  • Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

  • Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.

The Compute team works on the design of our AI supercomputers, doing everything from workload modeling to influencing accelerator design. We’re leaning into our partnerships to make system and data center co-design an integral part of this process, and are looking for engineers to design AI supercomputers solutions for data center applications

This team is responsible for working with partners to optimize their hardware for our workloads, identifying promising new deep learning accelerators, and bringing those hardware platforms to production.

If you’re excited to work at the intersection of cutting edge deep learning, hardware system, and data center design this role is for you!

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks. You’ll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment. Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals.

  • Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers. Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements. Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance.

  • Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level.

  • Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing. Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress.

  • Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals. State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets.

  • Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause. Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring.

  • Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components. Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack.

  • Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods. Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners.

  • Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing. Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life.

  • Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces. Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life.

  • Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

  • Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews. Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners.

  • Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses.

  • Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams. Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans.

  • Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement. Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/HPC servers, networking equipment, or storage systems, spanning PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and integrated racks.

  • Have designed, instrumented, and executed hardware reliability tests, debugged failures in the lab, and translated results into practical design or process improvements.

  • Understand failure mechanisms in electronic assemblies, including solder fatigue, PCB and laminate damage, connector wear, corrosion, and thermal or mechanical degradation.

  • Can turn mission profiles and failure risks into qualification plans, select defensible sample sizes and stress levels, and explain the assumptions and limits of accelerated testing.

  • Have led reliability qualification through development and production milestones, balancing sample availability, lab capacity, schedule, and the evidence needed for release decisions.

  • Have worked directly with component suppliers, joint design manufacturers, contract manufacturers, and external test labs to review test methods, resolve failures, and verify corrective actions.

  • Apply design for reliability, DFMEA, and physics-of-failure methods across electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces, and understand how manufacturing, assembly, handling, and repair affect long-term reliability.

  • Have driven structured failure analysis and corrective action using methods such as 8D, supported by electrical diagnostics, microscopy, X-ray, cross-section analysis, or specialist failure-analysis labs as appropriate.

  • Can analyze reliability and life-test data, including censored data, Weibull distributions, and confidence bounds, using tools such as Python, R, JMP, or equivalent statistical software.

  • Bring experience with high-power electronics, dense interconnects, or liquid-cooled hardware, including thermal interfaces, leak integrity, material compatibility, and serviceability.

  • Communicate technical findings and uncertainty clearly, distinguish verified root cause and corrective-action effectiveness from hypotheses, and prioritize reliability risks when requirements or designs change.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Dots is building personal AI agents that help people make progress on their goals, including when they are away from ChatGPT. These agents can learn preferences, maintain context, work across applications, and use cloud computers to carry out tasks.

Our team brings together product engineering, design, and research to turn frontier model capabilities into useful everyday experiences. We are defining how people delegate work, understand what an agent is doing, and stay in control. Engineers help shape both the product and the systems behind it, from early prototypes through launch and iteration.

About the Role

We are looking for Senior and Staff Full Stack Software Engineers to build Dots product experiences from the interface through the services that power them. You will help define how people delegate tasks to personal agents, follow their progress, and collaborate with them over time. This role combines hands-on product development with the systems work needed to make persistent, asynchronous agent experiences reliable.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and launch features across web interfaces, APIs, backend services, and data models.

  • Create workflows for task creation, progress updates, agent feedback, and results that remain coherent across sessions and devices.

  • Translate emerging model capabilities into product prototypes with research, product, and design partners.

  • Design clear interfaces between product surfaces and agent execution systems.

  • Improve performance and reliability across the stack, including user-facing latency and recovery from partial failures.

  • Own projects from early exploration through architecture, implementation, launch, and iteration based on user feedback.

  • Help establish technical direction, testing practices, and observability as the product grows.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience building and shipping products across frontend and backend systems.

  • Can move comfortably between user interfaces, service design, APIs, and data modeling.

  • Bring strong product instincts and care about making complex capabilities understandable to users.

  • Have taken ambiguous ideas from concept to production and made practical tradeoffs between iteration speed and long-term maintainability.

  • Understand asynchronous workflows and can reason about state, consistency, and failure across system boundaries.

  • Collaborate effectively with design, product, research, and engineering partners.

  • Have owned complex engineering projects and helped other engineers make sound technical decisions.

  • Experience launching new consumer products, building agent or workflow applications, or working in small teams with broad engineering ownership is especially relevant.

  • Prior experience with AI or machine learning is helpful, but not required. We welcome experienced engineers who want to bring strong product and engineering judgment to a new category of software.

raw_data.title: SoC Engineer
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.

About the Role

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.

In this role, you will:

  • Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

  • Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

  • Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

  • Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

  • Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure.

  • Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

  • Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

  • Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

  • Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

  • Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

  • Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

  • Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

  • Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

  • Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

  • Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

  • Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

  • Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

  • Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

  • Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug.

  • Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership.

  • Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work.

raw_data.title: Electrical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.


About the Role

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.


In this role, you will:

  • Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

  • Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

  • Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

  • Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

  • Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

  • Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

  • Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

  • Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

  • Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

  • Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

  • Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

  • Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

  • Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

  • Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.

Required qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

  • Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

  • Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

  • Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

  • Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

  • Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.

Preferred qualifications

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

  • Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet.

  • Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware.

What success looks like

  • Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer.

  • Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. Track false failures, cycle time, and uptime against agreed improvement targets.

  • Release hardware documentation, versioned test code, commissioning checks, and troubleshooting procedures that enable lab and contract-manufacturer teams to reproduce, operate, and maintain the station

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

 - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

 - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

 - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

 - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

 - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

 - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

 - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

 - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

 - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

 - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

 - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

 - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

 - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet.

 - Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer.

 - Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. Track false failures, cycle time, and uptime against agreed improvement targets.

raw_data.title: Software Engineer, Mobile Web — Dots
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Dots is building personal AI agents that help people make progress on their goals, including when they are away from ChatGPT. These agents can learn preferences, maintain context, work across applications, and use cloud computers to carry out tasks.

Our team brings together product engineering, design, and research to turn frontier model capabilities into useful everyday experiences. We are defining how people delegate work, understand what an agent is doing, and stay in control. Engineers help shape both the product and the systems behind it, from early prototypes through launch and iteration.

About the Role

We are looking for Senior and Staff Software Engineers to build the mobile web experience for Dots. You will create responsive, accessible interfaces that let people start work, follow progress, and guide their agents from a phone or browser. You will help establish interaction patterns for ongoing, asynchronous work and make sophisticated agent capabilities feel clear and approachable.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and ship mobile web experiences for creating tasks, reviewing agent activity, and providing feedback or direction.

  • Build interfaces that handle streaming updates, long-running tasks, interrupted sessions, and changing connectivity.

  • Improve responsiveness, loading performance, accessibility, and usability across screen sizes and browsers.

  • Partner with design and product to prototype interaction patterns that give users visibility and control over agent actions.

  • Work with backend and full stack engineers on APIs, client state, and reliable synchronization between the interface and agent services.

  • Own features from exploration and technical design through launch, measurement, and refinement.

  • Help set frontend architecture and engineering practices while staying hands-on with implementation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial experience shipping polished web applications, with deep expertise in mobile web development and browser behavior.

  • Bring strong frontend engineering skills and understand responsive layouts, accessibility, client state, and application performance.

  • Have built interactive interfaces that stay understandable as data or task state changes asynchronously.

  • Combine attention to visual and interaction details with sound technical judgment.

  • Can turn ambiguous product problems into working software and use user feedback to improve it.

  • Work well with designers, product partners, researchers, and engineers across the stack.

  • Have led complex projects or influenced architecture while continuing to write and ship code.

  • Experience with real-time collaboration, offline or intermittent connectivity, or products that help users manage complex workflows is especially relevant.

  • Prior experience with AI or machine learning is helpful, but not required. We welcome experienced engineers who want to bring strong product and engineering judgment to a new category of software.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Preparedness Engineering team is responsible for building and operating safeguards for frontier model risks, to safely enable advanced capabilities while detecting and limiting harm.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead a team building software systems that detect and prevent harmful misuse of frontier AI models—before incidents occur. This is a builder’s role: you’ll lead engineers shipping production services, detection pipelines, and mitigation mechanisms that protect frontier model integrity and reduce high-severity misuse risk.

While this work intersects with frontier model development, security and risk, we’re explicitly seeking someone with a software engineering foundation who is comfortable building reliable systems that can operate at billions of users scale.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead a team of software engineers building detection + mitigation systems for frontier model harms.

  • Set the technical roadmap and execution strategy: prioritize, design, ship, iterate, measure impact.

  • Build production systems: services, pipelines, tooling, instrumentation, and automation that scale with frontier model usage.

  • Partner deeply with Research and Product to translate evolving model capabilities into concrete tests, signals, and mitigations that can be deployed at scale.

  • Drive strong engineering fundamentals: architecture, reliability, monitoring, performance, and operational excellence.

  • Hire and grow an exceptional team across backend, data systems, and applied ML engineering domains as needed.

  • Anticipate what breaks at scale as agentic workflows become more capable.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Experience building systems in adversarial, fast-evolving environments

  • Thrive in high context environments

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and novelty

  • Communicate clearly and build trust quickly with senior stakeholders—pragmatic, collaborative, and calm under scrutiny.

  • Significant experience leading engineering teams and delivering production systems end-to-end.

  • Strong technical judgment in system design, distributed systems, data pipelines, observability, and operational reliability.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with Research/Product/Security to ship systems that materially reduce risk or abuse at scale.

  • Background in autonomy, high-scale real-time systems, or intelligence-adjacent technical domains is a plus.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering team builds and operates the platforms that make employee devices secure, reliable, and easy to use. Our work spans device posture and trust, onboarding, application delivery, operating-system updates, fleet telemetry, and employee-facing remediation. We partner with Security, IT, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering teams to reduce friction while protecting OpenAI’s systems and data.

About the Role

As a Client Platform Engineer, You will build and own agentic solutions that automate OAI fleet operations and reduce employee friction, with measurable outcomes and reliability. You will develop first-party software, integrate commercial and open-source tools, and own changes from design and testing through deployment and production operations. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role.

In this role, you will:

Build the platforms that help employees do their best work on devices they can trust.

  • Own the design, development, deployment, and operation of secure Linux endpoint management systems across environments with different compliance requirements.

  • Create magical employee experiences by building agentic workflows with OpenAI products and models that use fleet telemetry to anticipate issues, guide remediation, and design friction out of everyday work.

  • Make new hires productive from day one, using OpenAI products to simplify device setup, software delivery, and onboarding support.

  • Build secure, reliable workflows with scoped access, human review for sensitive changes, traceable actions, and tested recovery.

  • Partner with IT, Security, Research, and Engineering to deliver consistent Linux provisioning, updates, and support alongside macOS and Windows.

  • Develop first-party software and integrate commercial and open-source tools for software packaging, deployment, and application management.

  • Manage fleet configuration as code through GitOps, version control, peer review, and automated validation.

  • Build and operate CI/CD pipelines for fleet infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and GCP, with staged deployments and tested rollback.

  • Use fleet telemetry to proactively improve performance and reliability, detect configuration drift, and verify deployment outcomes.

  • Participate in engineering on-call, own incident resolution, and turn operational lessons into lasting improvements that reduce recurring failures and manual work.

You may be a fit for this role if you have: 

  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or another modern programming language.

  • Deep experience securing and managing Linux fleets with configuration management, MDM, device enrollment, policy enforcement, and cloud identity integration.

  • Demonstrated success with open-source endpoint tools for configuration, device and application management, and telemetry.

  • Experience delivering secure, reliable, scalable systems across different compliance requirements.

  • Deep experience managing infrastructure at scale with IaC and GitOps, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and Chef.

  • Experience integrating and operating fleet infrastructure with CI/CD and DevOps workflows.

  • A track record of deploying and operating fleet infrastructure in public cloud environments (Azure, AWS, GCP).

  • Initiative, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn problems into practical improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Deep experience with open-source fleet management tools and frameworks.

  • Experience with containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and NIST.

  • Strong soft skills, including stakeholder communication and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CCSP.

  • A security thought leader with contributions to CPE open-source projects or technical communities.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Enterprise Security protects the systems, identities, devices, and services that enable OpenAI's employees to work securely and effectively. We partner across IT and Security to understand risk, build practical defenses, and support a rapidly evolving technical environment.

About the Role

We are looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer with a focus on vulnerability management, novel vulnerabilities, and zero-day response. You will investigate vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across networks, endpoints, and SaaS, prioritize them in the context of real exposure, and drive remediation through verified outcomes.

You will also build security capabilities and automation, use AI agents to solve practical problems, and help shape how enterprise security operates as agents become a larger part of everyday work.

This role is open to candidates in San Francisco, CA, and to remote candidates in the United States.

In this role, you will:

  • Discover, investigate, and prioritize vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across enterprise systems, including novel vulnerabilities and zero-days with incomplete information and no established playbook.

  • Translate technical findings into clear attack paths, business impact, and actionable remediation.

  • Develop and validate emergency mitigations when patches are unavailable, coordinate with system owners, vendors, and incident responders, and drive durable fixes through verified closure.

  • Improve asset visibility, ownership, vulnerability data quality, and reporting.

  • Build and operate security tools and integrations using code, APIs, automation, and AI agents.

  • Design controls for agent access, execution, and accountability.

  • Contribute across endpoint, network, identity, and SaaS security, and support incident investigations when needed.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have independently investigated novel or emerging vulnerabilities and driven enterprise remediation from uncertain initial reports through mitigation and verified closure.

  • Bring technical depth in a relevant security domain and working knowledge across networks, endpoints, and SaaS.

  • Can understand and improve code and safely integrate APIs and security systems.

  • Have solved substantive problems using AI agents and can explain how you evaluated and corrected their work.

  • Think clearly about security tradeoffs, ambiguous evidence, and the changing risks of agentic systems.

  • Collaborate effectively, take ownership, and communicate technical risk to varied audiences.

raw_data.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) - AI Infra - SF
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers lead complex deployments of frontier models in production. You will embed with customers where model performance matters, delivery is urgent, and ambiguity is the default. You will use this to map their problems, structure delivery, and ship fast. 

As a Forward Deployed Engineer for AI Infra, you will work directly with customer engineers, researchers and product engineers on optimization problems across semiconductors and AI infrastructure. You will write and debug software, run experiments against real workloads and hardware, and improve the tools and product used across engagements.

You will help define the problem and success criteria, build the software needed to test an approach, and stay with the work through validation and deployment. Work may include inference performance and chip-design optimization. Success means producing results that stand up to correctness and performance checks, and contributing improvements that other engagements can use.

Success in this role means owning the delivery state across workstreams. You will hold the bar on quality and pace and help OpenAI learn through execution.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Own technical delivery for agreed semiconductor and AI-infrastructure workstreams, from initial scoping and prototypes through validation, production deployment and adoption.

  • Work closely with customer engineers to understand their workflows and constraints, define workloads, baselines and success criteria, and help what you build become part of how they work.

  • Scope and sequence delivery, identify dependencies and blockers early, and make practical trade-offs between scope, speed and quality as the work develops.

  • Personally build and debug production-quality software, including harnesses, integrations and product features that apply frontier models to problems in chip design, verification, inference and performance engineering.

  • Design reproducible experiments, evaluations, graders and benchmarks to test approaches, validate correctness and performance, and establish whether improvements hold up in real engineering environments.

  • Investigate model behavior and failure modes alongside researchers, contributing evaluation or training data and targeted experiments where they can improve the underlying capability.

  • Contribute directly to core product development, working with product engineers to resolve tooling gaps, ship useful improvements and bring field learning into product decisions.

  • Lead technical discussions and maintain alignment across customer, Product and Research teams. Build the domain and product fluency to explain capabilities, limitations and results, and keep ownership, risks and next steps clear.

  • Turn successful approaches into reusable software, tools and playbooks, reducing the effort needed for future engagements and helping customer teams operate what has been built.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience that includes customer-facing work

  • Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous environments

  • Write and review production-grade software, and debug unfamiliar systems across code, integrations and runtime behavior.

  • Have built or deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behaviour affects product experience

  • Simplify complexity and make fast, sound decisions under pressure

  • Communicate clearly with engineers, product teams, and customer stakeholders

  • Spot risks early and adjust without slowing down

  • Model calm and judgment when the stakes are high

  • Have a strong product sense and have contributed towards productizing efforts

  • Have hands-on experience with applied machine learning, model evaluation, data quality, experimentation, or model-behavior analysis

  • Can turn an ambiguous technical problem into a clear evaluation, a credible baseline, and a reproducible experiment

  • Are comfortable learning unfamiliar technical domains and working closely with researchers, product engineers and customer engineers. Experience in semiconductor development, data-center systems or inference engineering is helpful.

raw_data.title: Software Engineer, TPU Compilers
raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Inference team brings OpenAI’s most capable research and technology to the world through our products. We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they’ve never been able to before. We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.

In this role, you will:

  • Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.

  • Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.

  • Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.

  • Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.

  • Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.

  • Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.

  • Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.

  • Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.

  • Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.

  • Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.

  • Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.

  • Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.

raw_data.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

Dots is looking for a Backend Engineer to build the systems that power our product. You’ll work closely with product, design, and engineering to turn ideas into reliable services and deliver features from design through production.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Paris. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

  • Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

  • Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

  • Are fluent in both French and English

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

  • Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

You’ll build the platforms and workflows our support teams rely on, including Salesforce Service Cloud. The work spans new capabilities, ongoing maintenance, automation, and reliability.

You’ll identify needs, clarify scope, make technical decisions, and carry work through implementation, testing, production validation, and ongoing operation. You’ll work closely with government, support, operations, Security, and engineering partners to understand constraints and deliver systems that work well in practice.

  • Own government support systems from problem definition through design, delivery, production validation, and ongoing operation. Turn ambiguous needs into clear priorities and practical technical plans.

  • Partner with government, support, operations, security, and engineering teams to make technical tradeoffs and translate access, data-handling, and change-control requirements into working solutions.

  • Improve reliability and performance through automated tests, observability, safe releases, incident response, and recovery. Validate changes in production and address recurring failure modes.

  • Document architecture, operational procedures, and recovery paths so systems are understandable and supportable. Automate repetitive work and contribute to other GASS priorities as needed.

You might thrive in this role if you have:
